key_insight: Agent-generated patches often fix the reported compiler example, but true success requires generalizing to the broader class of missed optimizations developers intended to cover.
engineering_relevance: For compiler teams, this shows that AI patching tools should be judged by optimization scope and correctness across similar IR cases, not just by whether they pass the original test.
method: Built a benchmark from real LLVM missed-optimization issues.
Compared agent-generated patches against developer patches by optimization scope.
Added historical-knowledge augmentation using retrieval and distillation from prior LLVM optimization pull requests.
evidence_signal: The study evaluates agent patches on real-world LLVM issues and reports that many patches only partially overlap with developer-intended scope, while some over-generalize beyond the reference fix.
watch_item: Historical retrieval can improve alignment, but over-generalization remains a risk and must be checked carefully before merging into compiler code.
paper_title: Understanding Agent-Based Patching of Compiler Missed Optimizations
